'''''Cassia leptophylla''''' is a tropical tree species in the genus ''[[Cassia (genus)|Cassia]]'', which is [[indigenous (ecology)|indigenous]] to [[Brazil]]. It is named '''gold medallion tree''' and has yellow flowers that bloom intermittently throughout the year, spawning [[seedpod]]s that are rectangular in cross section and rattle festively. It is recognized by its thin green [[foliage]] with glossy green pinnate leaflets. The fruit is a long thin seedpod with four sides.

==Native distribution==
''Cassia leptophylla'' is native to southeastern Brazil.<ref name=grin/>

==Uses==
This tree does not have many uses, except as a decorative tree or as a [[laxative]], something common to the genus ''Cassia''.

==Warning==
Seeds are poisonous if ingested. Parts of the plant are poisonous if ingested.
